newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel price into China plunges.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel price into China plunges.

text.p: Gas oil prices to China have plummeted by at least $40 in about two weeks with a recent sale of 30,000 tonnes at $216 a tonne cost-and-freight basis, traders said on Monday.
This reflected the bearish regional market with free-on-board (fob) Singapore prices falling to under $27.50 per barrel on Monday, with the bottom still not yet in sight, traders said.
Trades done into China about a month ago were as high as $260-$263 c-and-f.
Traders said some Chinese end users, realising they had paid too high a price earlier compared with current prices, have decided to default on their commitments.
This has left at least three traders and a major with "distressed cargoes on the water", sources said.
February gas oil swaps fell sharply late in the day as a result of the lower physical offers, to be quoted at $26.50/$26.75 per barrel from Friday's $27.15/$27.25.

But the weak physical undertone and another $5.50-a-tonne plunge in gas oil futures on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE), after losing $3.00 on Friday, was likely to depress the market further, they said.

Physical gas oil for early February lifting was offered lower on Monday from Friday's $27.50 and $28.25. On Monday, a trader offered at $26.85 while a major offered as low as $27.00 fob, with no buyers in sight.
Traders said Indonesia has started to buy "bits and pieces" of gas oil for February deliveries from traders, with most of the cargoes coming from the Middle East rather than Singapore.
Sellers assessed gas oil premiums at around 20 cents per barrel to Singapore spot quotes, fob.
They assessed jet fuel premiums at around 35 cents per barrel to Singapore spot quotes fob. A 100,000-to-120,000-barrel parcel of jet fuel was traded late last week at a 30-cent premium fob.
